passage:
I'm Nakul, and I was on the sofa while my cousin Mridul played online in our flat. He kept grinning at the screen. "An older player gave me a rare skin for free. He says I'm the best he's met, and I should add him on a private chat."
Then Mridul hesitated. "He also said not to tell my parents, because they'd make me stop." His grin dropped a little.
I asked, "Why would a grown-up give free stuff to a kid and want it kept secret?" He shrugged and said the skin was cool, but he didn't look sure.
Later I saw him remove the friend request. At dinner he told his mother. She put down her spoon, thanked him for telling her and said it wasn't his fault. They blocked and reported the account together that evening. I don't know whether he was scared or just tired of it.

qa.q: What did the older player give Mridul for free?
qa.a: He gave Mridul a rare skin.

qa.q: What did Mridul seem to be feeling when he hesitated?
qa.a: His grin dropped a little and he didn't look sure, so he seemed uneasy about the gift and the secrecy, though Nakul can't know for certain.

qa.q: What could Mridul do when someone offers gifts that come with secrecy?
qa.a: He can refuse gifts that come with secrecy, remove the contact and tell his parents or another trusted adult, as he did at dinner.

qa.q: How did Mridul's mother react when he told her at dinner?
qa.a: She stayed calm, thanked him for telling her and said it wasn't his fault, then blocked and reported the account with him that same evening.

grounding: Shows a teen offered gifts by an older gaming contact who asks for secrecy, and choosing to refuse and tell his mother.

passage:
Week one. In the online racing game, a player called "Maverick_29" started gifting Farida rare car skins. "You're a great racer. Take it, I have too many." She felt flattered. Her friend Usha said, "Who gives stuff to strangers for free?"

Week two. More gifts. Then messages: "You're my favourite teammate. Can I ask how old you are?" Farida told him fifteen. He said he was twenty-six. Then: "Let's chat on a private app instead. Keep it between us, the game mods are nosy." Farida felt a prickle of unease.

Week three. Maverick sent a message: "I got you the gold car you wanted. But this one's special. Don't mention it to your parents, okay?" Farida stared at it. Why would a grown man give a teenager so many gifts and want it secret?

She didn't accept the car. She blocked him and showed the whole chat to her mother that evening. Her mother saved the messages, reported the account to the game and sat with her. "You saw what he was doing. Good."

qa.q: How old did Maverick say he was?
What was Farida feeling when Maverick asked to keep the gift secret?
qa.a: Farida felt uneasy and suspicious, wondering why a grown man would give a teenager so many gifts and want it hidden.

qa.q: What did Farida do in week three, and why was it right?
qa.a: Farida refused the gift, blocked Maverick and showed her mother, because gifts tied to secrecy from an adult are a warning sign.

qa.q: How did Usha see the gifts from the start?
qa.a: Usha was suspicious from the start, doubting that anyone gives expensive things to strangers for free.

grounding: It shows a teen offered gifts in an online game by an older user who asks for secrecy, noticing why an adult would do this and refusing gifts that come with secrets.

passage:
Sharmila, you're getting free gems in that game from someone older? Let your Elizabeth Aunty tell you something from when I was fourteen.

We had chatrooms then. A man in one of them, he said he was a college student, kept sending me things. Music CDs by post. A phone recharge. Then a watch. I felt so grown up. Special.

He always said the same thing: "This is just between us. Your parents won't understand." I didn't tell anyone. The gifts made me feel like I owed him something.

One day he asked me to meet him at the bus depot to "get the next present in person." Something in me went cold.

I showed my mother the letters and the watch that night. She wasn't angry with me at all. She went to the police the next morning, and it turned out he had done this to three other girls.

That's why I'm asking, Sharmila. When a grown-up gives a teenager gifts and asks for secrets, it's never really a gift.

qa.q: What did the man send young Elizabeth after the phone recharge?
What was young Elizabeth feeling when he asked to meet at the bus depot?
qa.a: She felt a sudden cold fear, sensing that the gifts and secrets had been leading somewhere dangerous.

qa.q: What was the key choice in Elizabeth Aunty's story, and why did it matter?
qa.a: Showing her mother the letters and watch that night was key, because a trusted adult could go to the police and stop him.

qa.q: How did the gifts make young Elizabeth feel towards the man?
qa.a: The gifts made her feel special and grown up, but also as if she owed him something, which is how he kept her quiet.

grounding: It shows an elder recalling an older man who gave her gifts online and asked for secrecy, and explaining why a teen should never accept gifts that come with secrets.
